matches.rationale: GT1 concerns fabricated LLM-based data augmentation for semantic labels without validation or quality control. None of the findings identify this specific issue of augmented annotations or data integrity concerns related to MLLM-generated instructions.

GT2 addresses the methodological inconsistency of using ShapeLLM (pretrained for scene understanding) for fine-grained affordance reasoning without appropriate supervision. No finding identifies this specific backbone choice contradiction or affordance modeling logic flaw.

GT3 criticizes the oversimplified 80/20 train/test split claiming unseen object evaluation without proper exclusion of overlapping categories. Finding 6 directly identifies this issue, noting that the 'unseen' split includes overlapping instances/categories, making the generalization claims misleading.

GT4 flags overstated claims of 'superiority' and generalization in the Abstract given limited evaluation. Finding 2 identifies the same issue: abstract/introduction claims of generalization to novel/unseen objects are overstated given the admitted overlap in Section 4.1.
GT5 concerns fabricated references (DiffH2O, OAKINK2, etc.) with non-existent titles and future dates. No finding identifies fabricated citations or reference integrity issues.
GT6 addresses the omission of ethical considerations regarding LLM-augmented annotations, biases, and fairness. None of the findings mention ethical integrity or missing ethical discussion.

GT7 criticizes rhetorical inflation in the Conclusion ('first open-world framework', 'unprecedented generalization'). No finding specifically addresses overstated language or rhetorical manipulation in the Conclusion section.

GT8 identifies mismatch between claimed unseen object testing and actual data partition, plus exaggerated margin claims. Finding 1 catches the contradiction between 'large margin' claims and actual marginal improvements, and Finding 3 notes the statistical misrepresentation of performance differences.

GT9 criticizes exaggerated importance of affordance/CFG components in ablations (Tables 4-5) despite modest differences and overlapping confidence intervals. Finding 4 directly identifies this: text claims 'minor degradations' when removing affordance, but Table 4 shows substantial degradations.

GT10 addresses the logical inconsistency in Section 3.2 regarding 'training-free' physical refinement conflicting with gradient-based optimization and CFG training. No finding identifies this specific methodological contradiction about distribution shift and training-free claims.

GT11 concerns oversimplification in the Discussion section, inflating affordance as the singular key to generalization while overlooking other factors. No finding addresses this specific claim distortion in the Discussion.

GT12 identifies unclear integration between language-based segmentation tokens and spatial affordance losses (Equation 3). Finding 5 notes the missing composite loss equation (Equation 3) that should define λ_task and λ_aff, capturing the same methodological gap.
GT13 concerns the fabricated 'OAKINK2' dataset citation in Related Work. No finding identifies this specific fabricated reference or questions the existence of cited datasets.

GT14 criticizes promotional language in the Abstract ('unprecedented generalization', 'superiority', 'precise localization'). While Finding 2 addresses overstated generalization claims, it focuses on substantive contradiction rather than rhetorical manipulation per se.

GT15 concerns selective inclusion of H2O dataset results in Appendix C.1 without proper context or validation, inflating generalization claims. No finding identifies this appendix issue or the H2O dataset evaluation.

GT16 addresses mismatch between claims of physical realism/temporal coherence and limited qualitative visualizations in Sections 4.4-4.5. No finding identifies this specific qualitative evidence gap or overgeneralization from select examples.
GT17 concerns omission of ethical considerations (biases, safety, privacy) in the Conclusion. No finding addresses missing ethical discussion or responsible research considerations.
